title: US States
description: Click anywhere inside the correct state for full points!

rounds.clue: The largest US state by area, it spans four time zones and contains 17 of the 20 highest peaks in the country.
The only US state made entirely of islands, its hula dancing and surfing culture draws millions of visitors each year.
Home to BBQ brisket, the Alamo, and a state so large it has its own power grid separate from the rest of the country.
Shaped like a mitten, this state is the birthplace of the automobile industry and Motown music.
The smallest US state by area, it's known for its clam chowder, colonial history, and the famous Newport mansions.
Known as the Sunshine State, this peninsula is home to Disney World, alligators, and more lightning strikes than anywhere else in the US.
The birthplace of jazz and Mardi Gras, this state's cuisine — gumbo, beignets, crawfish étouffée — is unlike anywhere else in America.
This state is home to the most active volcano in the world, the deepest lake in the US, and more coastline than any other contiguous state.
The nation's most populous state, home to Hollywood, Silicon Valley, and more farmland than Iowa.
Known for its potatoes, this state is also the gem stone capital of the US and home to the deepest river gorge in North America.
The Centennial State, its Rocky Mountain peaks include 53 summits over 14,000 feet, and it was a pioneer in legalizing recreational cannabis.
Home to the Grand Canyon, the Painted Desert, and the Saguaro cactus — a symbol found nowhere else in the world.
The Land of Enchantment, this state has the highest percentage of Hispanic residents and was home to the Trinity nuclear test site.
Known as the Beehive State, it's home to five national parks, the Great Salt Lake, and the headquarters of the LDS church.
The Treasure State, it has more cattle than people, borders Canada, and contains the headwaters of the Missouri River.
This state grows more wheat than any other in the US and was the site of the deadliest single-building terrorist attack before 9/11.
The Sunflower State, this flat-as-a-pancake Great Plains state leads the US in helium production and was home to the famous Dodge City cattle drives.
Known as the Cornhusker State, it's the only state with a unicameral legislature and borders six other states.
The Mount Rushmore State, it's home to Crazy Horse Memorial, the Badlands, and the annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally.
The Peace Garden State, it has more lakes than Minnesota (by some counts) and produces more honey than any other US state.
The Land of 10,000 Lakes (actually over 11,000), this state is the birthplace of Bob Dylan and Prince.
The Hawkeye State, it's the top corn and pork producer in the US and holds the first presidential nominating caucuses.
The Show-Me State, birthplace of Mark Twain, home to the Gateway Arch — the tallest monument in the US.
The Land of Lincoln, this state's deep-dish pizza, hot dogs, and the Chicago Bears rivalry with the Green Bay Packers define its culture.
The Hoosier State, it hosts the world's greatest spectacle in racing — the Indianapolis 500 — every Memorial Day weekend.
The Buckeye State, this Midwestern powerhouse has produced more US presidents than any other state — eight in total.
The Great Lakes State's lower peninsula looks like a mitten, but its Upper Peninsula is known for pasties — a meat-filled pastry brought by Cornish miners.
America's Dairyland — this state produces more cheese than any other and is home to the Green Bay Packers, the only publicly owned NFL team.
The Volunteer State, home to the Grand Ole Opry, the country music capital of the world, and Jack Daniel's distillery.
The Bluegrass State, famous for thoroughbred horse racing, bourbon whiskey, and the world's longest known cave system.
The Mountain State, the only state formed by seceding from another state during the Civil War — it broke away from Virginia.
The Old Dominion, birthplace of eight US presidents including Washington, Jefferson, and Madison.
The Tar Heel State, home to the Wright Brothers' first flight at Kitty Hawk and the nation's most famous college basketball rivalry.
The Palmetto State, site of the first shots of the Civil War at Fort Sumter and home to the legendary Masters golf tournament (across the border, but the golfers live here).
The Peach State, home to Coca-Cola's birthplace, CNN headquarters, and the busiest airport in the world.
The Heart of Dixie, birthplace of the Civil Rights Movement — from the Montgomery Bus Boycott to the Selma to Montgomery marches.
The Magnolia State, birthplace of the blues along the Delta, Elvis Presley, and America's greatest river running along its western border.
The Natural State, home to Walmart's global headquarters, the Ozark Mountains, and Bill Clinton's presidential birthplace.
The Keystone State, birthplace of American democracy — the Constitution and Declaration of Independence were both signed here.
The Empire State, home to more people in its largest city alone than in many entire countries — and the world's most famous skyline.
The Garden State, the most densely populated state in the US and home to the original boardwalk at Atlantic City.
The Constitution State, it was the first to ratify the US Constitution and is home to more hedge funds per capita than anywhere else.
The Bay State, birthplace of John F. Kennedy and the Boston Red Sox, famous for its chowder, lobster rolls, and Harvard University.
The Green Mountain State, the first state to abolish adult slavery and the birthplace of Ben & Jerry's ice cream.
The Granite State, known for its 'Live Free or Die' motto, it holds the first primary election of every presidential race.
The Pine Tree State, the easternmost state in the continental US and the largest of New England's states, known for lobster and L.L.Bean.
The First State, the first to ratify the Constitution in 1787 and home to more corporations than any other state due to its business-friendly laws.
The Old Line State, home to the Chesapeake Bay — the largest estuary in the US — and the birthplace of Francis Scott Key.
The Silver State, known for Las Vegas, legal gambling, and Area 51 — it receives more visitors per resident than any other US state.
The Evergreen State, home to Microsoft, Amazon, Starbucks, and Boeing — arguably the most tech-and-coffee-obsessed state in the union.
